results.message: What did your church do for its dead?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text:
We offered the sacrifice at the altar on their behalf, and we gave alms in the church for them. Augustine taught that these gifts help only the baptized dead who earned that help in life. For the very good, the offerings are thanksgiving. For those not very bad, they ask God's favor on their behalf. For the very bad they do not help the dead at all, but they console the living. Augustine's mother, Monica, made one request as she lay ill: ““Lay this body anywhere. Do not let the care of it trouble you at all. I ask only this: that you remember me at the Lord’s altar, wherever you are.””

She did not care where her body was laid, only that we would keep her in mind at the Lord's table.

We taught the living too. Augustine had psalms of penance copied and hung on the wall beside his own deathbed, and wept over them. The man who said all merit is gained in this life showed us how a bishop prepares to meet the one he will answer to.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV, independently re-located this session; Doc_01 SS2); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII; Doc_01 SS2); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo (lpc.story.the-psalms-on-the-wall)
